operations.content: Step 2 complete: Read source files. main.cpp has custom heap manager with global operator overrides. user.cpp has only empty stub functions. Key hypothesis: object lifetime vs custom heap lifetime issue. Next: compile and run to confirm crash, then debug.
user.cpp current state: Contains only empty stub functions user_init(), user_cleanup(), and user_main() - essentially minimal implementation

main.cpp architecture: Uses CustomHeapManager (bump allocator) with global operator new/delete overrides. Custom heap created in init(), destroyed in shutdown(). shutdown() called from Application destructor which also calls user_cleanup() after heap destruction.
CustomHeapManager deallocate() does nothing (lines 61-67 of main.cpp) - it's a bump allocator that only frees entire heap on destruction. Individual objects aren't freed from the custom heap.

Hypothesis for release crash: Object lifetime issue. Standard library objects allocated during run() might outlive custom heap destruction in shutdown(). When operator delete is called after g_custom_heap is nullptr, it tries std::free() on memory from custom heap buffer, causing crash. Optimizer behavior differs between DEBUG (-O0) and RELEASE (-O2) affecting object lifetimes.
